html:
SMTO-HTTP-0057 — SMTO couldn't accept these connection settings

GUID: 3e58eab6-3645-4274-8629-2adfffe72f24
Slug: http-profile-input-invalid
Domain: HTTP · Subsystem: http

What happened

  • The web connection you were saving or opening has settings that are missing, unrecognized or in the wrong form, so it wasn't saved or couldn't be opened.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Open Parameter Store, select the connection, and choose Reveal & edit value. The editor shows the real saved values; the hidden preview can't be saved back.
  2. Check that Base URL is a complete web address, such as https://example.com, and that the Authentication section has the right type with every value filled in. SMTO needs a valid address and a complete sign-in method before it accepts the connection.
  3. Don't copy masked or hidden values from a preview into the fields. Type the real values, then select Save. Saving masked values would replace your real password or key with placeholder text.
  4. Select Test connection to confirm the saved settings work. The test confirms SMTO can read the settings and reach the service.

What success looks like

  • The connection saves without an error and Test connection reports it as Reachable.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO. Don't delete and recreate the connection just to clear this; its saved sign-in values would be lost.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • The HTTP connection route rejected the input: the body was not a JSON object, it contained fields other than profile, aliases, description and create, the profile failed validation, the connection was not found, or the saved profile could not be normalized for display.

What this means

  • The connection editor or management operation received malformed/non-object JSON, unsupported fields, a missing profile or invalid public profile/metadata. The specific receipt owns dispatch and effect truth. Authentication exchanges, resource requests and Gateway admission are separate phases; rendering this explanation performs no request and never authorizes replay of an uncertain mutation.

Why this can happen

  • The connection editor or management operation received malformed/non-object JSON, unsupported fields, a missing profile or invalid public profile/metadata.

How to diagnose it

  • Check allowed top-level fields and the typed public profile, including whether redacted preview data was mistakenly resubmitted.

How to fix it

  • Send only profile, aliases, description and create in the PUT body for the connection under /api/agent/http/connections/, with a valid http_connection profile (profile_type, profile_version, base_url, auth). For a stored profile that fails to open, reveal it in Parameter Store and replace its invalid public fields; never save redacted preview values in place of real credentials.
  • Use the HTTP connection editor’s supported authentication and TLS fields. Put credentials in its private credential flow; do not replace a connection with redacted preview values.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the recorded cause, then inspect current state and existing receipts before requesting another attempt.

How to verify the fix

  • The supported edit validates with private values kept in their designated flow.

What not to do

  • Do not repeatedly submit the same invalid input; correct the named constraint first.

Technical notes

  • The specific receipt owns dispatch and effect truth. Authentication exchanges, resource requests and Gateway admission are separate phases; rendering this explanation performs no request and never authorizes replay of an uncertain mutation.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
